summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of mesenteric fibromatosis and recurrent small bowel obstructions was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain consistent with prior flares. Imaging showed no mechanical obstruction, and symptoms were managed with NPO status, TPN, IV fluids, and pain and nausea control using IV Dilaudid and rectal morphine and Phenergan. She was advanced to clear liquids but redeveloped vomiting after attempting a regular diet, prompting reversion to clear liquids at discharge with instructions to advance slowly at home. A tear in the femoral TPN line hub was repaired via nonoperative intervention, and ethanol locks were initiated. Her chronic conditions, including migraines, hypothyroidism, anemia of chronic disease, and asthma, remained stable. She was discharged home on a clear liquid diet with updated PR medications for pain and nausea, instructions to resume TPN, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
